purpose: Test whether B12X-style N256 FC2 activation reuse is bit-exact and large enough to plausibly close the remaining P8-to-EXL3 decode gap.

candidate.fc2: one N256 task; A and SFA staged once per K128

decision_rule: Correctness requires identical payload and BF16 output hashes across arms on every GPU, five-run graph determinism, and graph/eager equality. Advance to integrated TP4 only if N256 is faster on every GPU and lowers graph median at least 35 percent on every GPU; otherwise profile or redesign without paying for another full-model run.
rationale_for_35_percent: The integrated N128 path is 17.168 percent below EXL3 and needs about 2.27 ms/token. With roughly 42 routed-layer calls, a small FC2-only gain is insufficient; the device gate is sized to the remaining product deficit.
codec_contract: K4 procedural MCG to E4M3, physical UE8M0/32, identity, mxf8f6f4, ordered monolithic per-K128 BF16 boundary
